# New house renderings proposed in odyssey-004 (Odyssey 1.325–444)

Additional rows for the conventions.md house-renderings table.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀμφίαλος Ἰθάκη (1.386, 395, 401) | "sea-girt Ithaca" | "sea-girt Ithaca" | "island-girt Ithaca", "encircled-by-sea Ithaca" (too free); literal sense is ἀμφί "around" + ἅλς "sea" |
| δῖα γυναικῶν (of Penelope, 1.332) | "heavenly-one of women" | "heavenly among women" | "bright among women", "shining among women" — kept parallel to the table's δῖα θεάων rather than treated as a separate formula |
| θεῖος (of Phemius, θεῖον ἀοιδόν, 1.336) | "divine" | "the divine minstrel" | "godlike" (reserved for ἀντίθεος/θεοειδής), "heavenly" (reserved for δῖος) |
| περίφρων Πηνελόπεια (1.329) | "circumspect Penelope" | "circumspect Penelope" | "wise Penelope", "prudent Penelope" (reserved for πεπνυμένος), "thoughtful Penelope" |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ Ἀντίνοος προσέφη, Εὐπείθεος υἱός (reply-formula: name + patronymic, no participle, 1.383) | "Him then in turn addressed Antinous, Eupeithes’ son:" | "Then Antinous, son of Eupeithes, spoke to him in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for τὸν/τὴν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα) |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύμαχος Πολύβου πάϊς ἀντίον ηὔδα (reply-formula: name + patronymic + ἀντίον ηὔδα, 1.399) | "Him then in turn spoke Eurymachus, Polybus’ son, face to face:" | "Then Eurymachus, son of Polybus, spoke to him in turn, face to face:" | "answered" (reserved for τὸν/τὴν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα) |
| κεδνὰ ἰδυῖα (of Eurycleia, 1.428) | "the one wise and trusty" | "trusty and wise" | "kindly", "careful" alone (loses ἰδυῖα "knowing, skilled") |
| αἰθομένας δαΐδας φέρε (repeated within this part, 1.428 = 1.434) | "burning torches carried" | "carried burning torches" | "blazing torches", "flaming brands" — kept to the same wording both occurrences per the repeated-line rule |

Notes:
- ἀμφίαλος Ἰθάκη, δῖα γυναικῶν, θεῖος (of a minstrel), and the two new name-and-patronymic reply-formulas (for Antinous and Eurymachus) are all near-certain to recur later in the poem and should be checked against these renderings when they do.
- κεδνὰ ἰδυῖα and the iterative imperfect in -σκε (φιλέεσκε, 1.435) are flagged here for consistency; the -σκε iterative itself is a recurring Homeric form rather than a lexical choice, so it has no table row, but later parts should keep glossing it the same way ("used to ...").
